questionsToConsider: What is the one sentence you want to test, and is it the same one that will appear on your website?
Are you testing one version, or sending different versions of the statement to different groups?
Which benefits are you really choosing between for your headline?
Do the respondents match the audience you plan to reach, or are they friends being kind?
guide.howToUseResponses: Read the explain-it-back answers before any score. If people describe something different from what you meant, fix the words before worrying about believability. Then compare the top-ranked benefit with the one your current headline leads with, and use the doubts and proof answers to decide what goes directly under it: reviews, a trial, a guarantee or clear pricing. The one-sentence descriptions are often better copy than the original.
customizeSteps: Replace the example in the statement with your own value proposition, written exactly as it will appear.
Rewrite the benefit and doubt options around your offer, keeping one neutral choice in each.
Duplicate the survey for each version you want to compare, and send each link to a similar group.

faqs.q: How do you test a value proposition?
faqs.a: Show the statement to people in your target audience, ask them to explain it back, then ask how relevant, believable and appealing it is. Misunderstandings in their own words are the fastest signal that the message needs work.

faqs.q: What questions should a value proposition survey ask?
faqs.a: What people think the offer does, how clear it is, how relevant it is to them, which benefit matters most, how believable the claim is and what would convince them.

faqs.q: Can I test two versions of my messaging?
faqs.a: Yes. Copy the survey, change the statement in the copy and send each version to a comparable group, then compare the results in the dashboard or a CSV export.

faqs.q: Why ask people to explain the offer in their own words?
faqs.a: A clarity score tells you people think they understood. Their own words show whether they actually did.

doc.title: Value proposition test
doc.description: Test whether your offer's promise is understood, relevant and believable before you build a campaign on it.

blocks.title: We're testing how we describe something new, and we'd value your honest first reaction. About three minutes.
Here's how we describe it: "Plan a week of dinners in ten minutes, with one shopping list and no wasted food."
blocks.description: Read it once, then answer the next few questions from memory.
